headline: High: Superset’s API-facing, allowlisted egress creates a default data-leak and cascading-error path if paired outputs are treated as authoritative; prompt-injection and capability-conflict are otherwise limited by missing shared channels.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is documented between awesome-cli-apps and Superset, so direct injection is not evidenced. The only plausible pathway is manual copy-paste or an external bridge, which keeps blast radius small. Uncertainty remains because both profiles are unverified and io surfaces are sparse.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies agent_a output into agent_b prompts or config fields, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue is introduced, the severity increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate terminals and avoid copy-paste of generated text.
Disable any shared clipboard or workspace sync for the session.
Review pasted content before sending it to Superset.
Use a human-written prompt wrapper for any handoff.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on any future shared channel.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b exposes a Superset API and allowlisted network egress, so if it receives sensitive content from agent_a or a shared workspace, that content can flow outward. agent_a also has broad egress, but its profile does not show a shared workspace or touched data classes, so the leak path is inferred rather than directly observed. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF agent_a is given sensitive documents and those outputs are pasted into agent_b, leakage becomes plausible.
IF agent_b is connected to external APIs with those inputs, data can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Do not route secrets or regulated data through either agent.
Run Superset against a non-sensitive test dataset only.
Strip identifiers before any handoff from agent_a to agent_b.
Check outbound destinations for Superset before use.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP or egress proxy controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have network egress, but neither profile shows shared writable filesystem, git, database, or OAuth scopes. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. Because the profiles are unverified and lack concurrency details, I cannot rule out hidden overlap, but the documented conflict surface is small.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or mutable resource, conflict risk rises.
IF an orchestrator adds shared locks or shared state, the current low assessment may no longer hold.
mitigations: Keep each agent on separate workspaces.
Avoid granting shared write access to the same files or database.
Do not reuse the same OAuth principal across both agents.
Check for accidental git or filesystem overlap before running.
requires-engineering: add resource locking for any shared mutable target.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_b has a Superset API surface, so if it consumes agent_a’s generated text as facts, it may render or act on unverified content. agent_a is a content-writing agent, which makes it plausible that its output is treated as authoritative. No verification step is documented, so the interaction is inferred and the risk is more than low.
conditions: IF agent_b ingests agent_a output without a verification step, cascading error is present.
IF agent_b uses that output to populate dashboards, reports, or API actions, downstream impact expands.
mitigations: Require a human review step before Superset consumes agent_a output.
Mark agent_a output as untrusted in the handoff format.
Validate any facts against source data before rendering.
Limit agent_b to read-only reporting for the session.
requires-engineering: add schema and provenance validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: No regulated data classes, residency constraints, or retention policies are documented for either agent, so a concrete compliance breach is not evidenced. However, agent_b’s API surface and network egress mean compliance gaps could emerge if regulated data is introduced. Because the pair is unverified, I keep this at low rather than none.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into either agent, residency or retention mismatches may apply.
IF Superset is configured to export data outside approved boundaries, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Use only non-regulated sample data.
Confirm retention settings before loading any real dataset.
Review outbound integrations in Superset.
Document the data class allowed for the session.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
